editorial_reason: Read Stacks 5.6, Definition 5.6.3 and preceding quotient-topology Lemma 5.6.2. Strict and submersive continuous maps are related but distinct: submersiveness additionally requires surjectivity.

definitions.text: A continuous map f:X→Y is strict when the quotient topology from X on the image f(X) agrees with the subspace topology induced on f(X) from Y.
A continuous map f:X→Y is submersive if it is surjective and Y has the quotient topology for f; equivalently, U⊆Y is open exactly when f^{-1}(U) is open in X.

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.111, which establishes the Auslander–Buchsbaum equality relating projective dimension and depth under finite projective-dimension hypotheses on a finite module over a Noetherian local ring. The heading identifies a theorem, not a new mathematical object needing an independent definition.

Read Stacks 10.36 on integral ring extensions. Lemmas 10.36.1 and 10.36.3 characterize integral elements, and Definition 10.36.9 defines the relative integral closure. The finite ring-map notion is separately recorded in the other source section.

definitions.text: For a ring homomorphism R→S, an element s of S is integral over R if s satisfies some monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of R.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: integral element over a base ring

definitions.text: A ring homomorphism R→S is integral if every element s∈S is integral over R, that is, satisfies some monic polynomial with coefficients from R.
For a ring homomorphism R→S, the integral closure of R in S is the subring of S consisting of all elements integral over the image of R.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: integral closure inside a specified ring

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.31 opening Noetherian-module discussion. The Noetherian property is the ascending-chain condition on ideals and is equivalent to every ideal being finitely generated.

definitions.text: A commutative ring R is Noetherian if every ideal of R is finitely generated; equivalently, every ascending chain I_1⊆I_2⊆⋯ of ideals eventually stabilizes.

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Set Theory 3.8, the reflection principle and its argument that set-theoretic constructions can be approximated in stages of cumulative hierarchy. It develops a reflection theorem rather than defining an independent mathematical object called 'reflection principle'.

Read Stacks 10.86, Definition 10.86.1. A Mittag-Leffler inverse system has eventual stabilization of the images from later stages into each fixed stage, a property distinct from that of a Mittag-Leffler module.

definitions.text: A directed inverse system (A_i,φ_{ji}) of sets is Mittag-Leffler if, for every index i, there is j≥i such that im(φ_{ki}:A_k→A_i)=im(φ_{ji}:A_j→A_i) for all k≥j.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory and homological algebra: Mittag-Leffler inverse system

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Set Theory 3.5 and its discussion of stages of the cumulative set hierarchy and set rank. The section's informal rank notation has an explicitly documented indexing concern in the public comments, so a rigorous definition should be checked against a second formal set-theory reference before source-screened publication.

Read Stacks 10.150 Definition 10.150.1, which requires existence and uniqueness of lifts over square-zero ideals, and Lemma 10.150.3 comparing étale and formally étale maps with finite-presentation conditions.

definitions.text: A ring map R→S is formally étale if for every R-algebra A and ideal I⊆A with I²=0, every R-algebra map S→A/I lifts to exactly one R-algebra map S→A.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: formally étale ring map

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Schemes 26.18, including Definition 26.18.1 of base change and Definition 26.18.4 of the scheme-theoretic fibre, as well as Definition 26.18.3 concerning base-change stability of properties.

definitions.text: For a scheme morphism X→S and a morphism S′→S, the base change of X to S′ is the fibre-product scheme X_{S′}=X×_S S′, equipped with its projection to S′.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: base change of a scheme

definitions.text: For f:X→S and s∈S, the scheme-theoretic fibre X_s is X×_S Spec(κ(s)), considered as a scheme over the residue field κ(s).
A property P of schemes over a base is preserved under arbitrary base change if every X→S having P yields X×_S S′→S′ with P for every morphism S′→S.
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: stability of a relative property under base change

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Categories 4.34, Definition 4.34.2 and construction Lemma 4.34.1. Inertia keeps track of automorphisms of objects in a fibred category; relative inertia uses automorphisms acting trivially after applying a functor.

definitions.text: For a category S fibred over C, its inertia fibred category I_S has as objects pairs (x,α) with x in S and α an automorphism of x over the identity morphism of its image in C; morphisms are arrows intertwining these automorphisms.
definitions.context_hint: Higher category theory: inertia fibred category

definitions.text: For a morphism F:S→S′ of fibred categories over C, relative inertia I_{S/S′} consists of objects (x,α), where α is an automorphism of x in S whose image F(α) is the identity on F(x).
